    • endpoint

      public BiltNexoTerminalClient.Builder endpoint(String endpoint)
      Set the full terminal endpoint URL (e.g. https://192.168.1.100:8443/nexo).

    • connectTimeout

      public BiltNexoTerminalClient.Builder connectTimeout(Duration connectTimeout)
      Set the TCP connect timeout. Default is 10 seconds.

    • readTimeout

      public BiltNexoTerminalClient.Builder readTimeout(Duration readTimeout)
      Set the read timeout (time waiting for the terminal to respond). Default is 120 seconds, which accommodates cardholder interaction during payment transactions.

    • pingInterval

      public BiltNexoTerminalClient.Builder pingInterval(Duration pingInterval)
      Set the interval at which the client sends keep-alive pings to the terminal while a connection is held open. Use this to detect a dead terminal during long waits (e.g. cardholder interaction) rather than blocking until the read timeout elapses.

      Pings are HTTP/2 PING frames, so this only has an effect when the connection is negotiated as HTTP/2 via ALPN; on an HTTP/1.1 connection the interval is ignored. Duration.ZERO (the default) disables pinging.

      If the terminal does not acknowledge a ping within the interval, the connection is considered failed and the in-flight request fails with an IOException (surfaced as a BiltNexoClientException).

      Parameters:
      pingInterval - the ping interval, e.g. Duration.ofSeconds(1); Duration.ZERO disables pinging

    • disableRecoveryOnNetworkError

      public BiltNexoTerminalClient.Builder disableRecoveryOnNetworkError()
      Disable recovery of a request across transient network failures.

      Recovery is on by default. While on, each request is tagged with a stable X-Bilt-Request-Id correlation UUID; if the connection is torn down by a transient network error while the request is in flight, the client re-sends the identical request (same id) with backoff until it obtains the response or the operation (read) timeout elapses. The terminal keys execution on the id and treats an already-seen id as a recovery rather than a new operation, so the underlying operation runs at most once no matter how many times the client re-attempts. (Only transient failures are retried; deterministic ones such as a TLS trust failure are surfaced immediately.)

      Recovery requires terminal-side support for the correlation protocol (see docs/network-error-recovery.md). Against a terminal that does not implement it, a re-send is treated as a new operation, which for a long-running request risks executing it more than once — call this to turn recovery off in that case.

      Turning recovery off also removes the keep-alive pingInterval(Duration) that recovery otherwise enables (unless a ping interval was set explicitly).

    • trustCertificate

      public BiltNexoTerminalClient.Builder trustCertificate(Path certificatePath)
      Add a trust anchor: trust the terminal's TLS certificate by supplying the certificate it chains to — in production this is the merchant or small-merchant-pool CA certificate, so every device leaf certificate issued under that CA is accepted.

      Unlike trustAllCertificates(), the TLS handshake chain is fully verified: only certificates that chain to one of the supplied anchors are accepted. Because Bilt terminals present a leaf certificate whose Subject Alternative Name is a synthetic, non-resolving hostname ({Model}-{Serial}.live.pos.bilt.com) while the client connects by IP address, pair this with expectedHostnamePattern(String) so the certificate identity is verified against the SAN rather than the connection address.

      This method may be called multiple times to add several anchors.

      Parameters:
      certificatePath - path to a PEM- or DER-encoded X.509 certificate
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the file cannot be read or parsed

      public BiltNexoTerminalClient.Builder trustCertificate(InputStream certificateStream)

    • environment

      public BiltNexoTerminalClient.Builder environment(BiltTerminalEnvironment environment)
      Verify the terminal's identity against the standard hostname pattern for the given Bilt environment, instead of matching the connection's IP address. Equivalent to expectedHostnamePattern( environment.hostnamePattern()).

      The caller must still trust the CA hierarchy for the same environment via trustCertificate(Path); production and staging use fully separate CA roots, so the trust anchor and the environment must agree.

      Parameters:
      environment - the deployment environment to scope trust to

    • expectedHostnamePattern

      public BiltNexoTerminalClient.Builder expectedHostnamePattern(String pattern)
      Verify the terminal's identity by matching the certificate's Subject Alternative Name (DNS entries, falling back to the Common Name) against the given pattern, instead of matching the connection's IP address.

      Bilt terminals are reached by IP address but present a leaf certificate carrying a synthetic, non-resolving hostname of the form {Model}-{Serial}.live.pos.bilt.com. Standard hostname verification would reject this because the connection host (the IP) never matches that name. Setting a pattern such as "*.live.pos.bilt.com" replaces the default verifier with one that accepts any terminal whose certificate name matches the pattern.

      The pattern supports a single leading wildcard label, e.g. "*.live.pos.bilt.com" matches "V240m-ABC123.live.pos.bilt.com" (one label before the suffix) but not "a.b.live.pos.bilt.com". A pattern without a wildcard is matched exactly. Matching is case-insensitive.

      This controls identity verification only; the certificate chain is still validated against the anchors added with trustCertificate(Path). It has no effect when trustAllCertificates() is set.

      Parameters:
      pattern - the expected SAN/CN pattern, e.g. "*.live.pos.bilt.com"
